NOTE: in the arXiv source Table 2 is 'Imaging data characteristics' (no positions; Table 1 = literature masses, Table 3 = marginalized masses); the position results are in §2.6.2 'Central positions' (arXiv numbering), Fig. 5 = 7-parameter posterior triangle plot (centre positions shown in WCS degrees, graphically only), Fig. 7 = 95% centre contours, Fig. 8 = 1/2-sigma contours with X-ray peaks; BCG coordinates in Appendix Table A1.

z_cl.quote: Throughout this paper we adopt the following cosmology: $\Omega_m=0.27$, $\Omega_\Lambda=0.73$, $\Omega_k=0$, and $H_0=70$~km~s$^{-1}$ Mpc$^{-1}$.  At mean cluster redshift $z=0.278$ we have $1^{\prime\prime}=4.25$ kpc

subcluster_value.location: §3.2.3 (2-D analysis, arXiv numbering) and Fig. 14 caption

I.type: NW NFW mass-centre (MCMC posterior centre of the A1758NW NFW halo; distortion+magnification)
I.quote: As in previous studies \citep{sevenmergers,ragozzine} we found no significant offsets between the BCGs and the mass centres. Those distances are $24_{-14}^{+10}$ and $30_{-18}^{+12}$ arcsec, for NW and NE, respectively. Thus, in both cases,  the BCG position is consistent with the halo mass centre within 95\% c.l.

uncertainty.value: +10/-14 (on the I-S separation, not on the I position itself)
uncertainty.quote: Those distances are $24_{-14}^{+10}$ and $30_{-18}^{+12}$ arcsec, for NW and NE, respectively.
uncertainty.caveat: Confidence level of the +10/-14 interval is not stated explicitly (paper elsewhere quotes 68% ranges for MCMC masses, Table 3). Positional contours: 95% in Fig. 7, 1 and 2 sigma in Fig. 8 - graphical only.

G.type: NW X-ray peak (Chandra, barycentre technique in 0.6x0.6 arcmin box)
G.quote: For A1758NW, the position of the X-ray peak emission is compatible with that of the BCG and the mass clump centre, considering the uncertainties. ; Fig. 8: "in NW the positions of the three components (BCG, mass peak and  X-ray peak) are compatible within $2\sigma$." ; method: "The peaks of the X-ray emission were determined by using the barycentre technique. It consists on a search for local maxima, around which we define a box of  $0.6 \times 0.6$ arcmin ($\sim$ the size of central brightest regions). The peak is then the intensity weighted average position."

S_candidates.label: A1758NW BCG (Table A1 galaxy ID 89, marked with star)
S_candidates.location: Appendix A, Table A1 (A1758N catalogue), row ID 89; caption: 'The galaxies marked with $^\star$ and $^\diamondsuit$ are the A1758NW e A1758NE BGCs respectively.'

notes: I is available only as an offset from the NW BCG (24 +10/-14 arcsec); G (NW X-ray peak) has no coordinates and no numerical offset - only 'compatible within 2 sigma' with BCG and mass centre. No luminosity-weighted centroid is tabulated (red-sequence density maps only graphical), so S = NW BCG from Appendix Table A1. No positional uncertainties for G or S and no instrument centroiding error stated. For context (not designated): NE mass centre is 96 +14/-15 arcsec from the NE X-ray peak and 30 +12/-18 arcsec from the NE BCG (13:32:52.0 +50:31:33.9, ID 113). Plate scale 4.25 kpc/arcsec (their cosmology). Pointer 'Table 2 & §3.2' does not match the arXiv numbering (§3.2 here is dynamical 1-D/2-D analysis of A1758N); Fig. 5 (triangle plot) does show the centre-position posteriors but only graphically.
